title: Autotriage Cheflet: lightweight taskify pipeline for support prechecks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: oncall and support engineers spend 6-12 minutes per incident running a set of repetitive preflight checks (service health, KV cache state, scheduler backlog, spot GPU pool saturation, recent rollout events) before deciding whether to follow a remediation runbook. Goal: build a tiny, auditable agent ("cheflet") that composes those prechecks into a deterministic task plan, surfaces recommended runbook tasks in the Console, and (for safe, low-risk fixes) can execute guarded steps with approval. Scope: minimal core checks for runtime and admin surfaces, generated runbook-as-task JSON that can be executed by the existing runlet runner. Non-goals: full automatic remediation for high-risk operations on first rollout; long-term learning/ML-driven triage (future iteration).
rationale: We need to reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for common operational categories without adding cognitive overhead for oncall. Prior runs of fully autonomous remediators introduced hard-to-reproduce state changes; a small, explainable cheflet that outputs structured tasks keeps actions auditable and reversible. Using the runbook-as-task format aligns with existing runlet tooling and minimizes integration work.
design_notes: Cheflet will be a stateless service invoked by the Console or an ops webhook that performs: 1) deterministic preflight probes (http health, GPU metrics, queue depth, KV cache hit ratio, latest model rollout status); 2) map probe results to a compact decision tree with templated runbook tasks; 3) emit a runbook-task bundle (JSON) with metadata: inputs, affected resources, estimated risk, and required approver role. Execution path will require RBAC checks against the caller and can mark tasks as "dry-run". Telemetry: emit an event per invocation (cheflet.request), probe metrics, task bundle hash, and outcome. Implementation will be a small Go service using existing telemetry libs and the runlet task schema. To reduce blast radius we will default to suggestions; auto-execute only idempotent, read-only tasks (roll log collection, cache priming) unless explicit approval provided.
tasks: Prototype cheflet binary that runs three core probes: runtime-health, kv-cache-metrics, and pool-utilization
Define runbook-task bundle schema extension: task.risk_level and task.approval_required
Add RBAC check in runlet-runner to honour approval_required flag
Console integration: cheflet suggestions panel with explainability lines and execute/approve buttons
Instrument telemetry events and dashboards for cheflet usage and success rates
Safety gating: security review and threat model for cheflet auto-execute paths
Migration: convert top-10 manual preflight checklist steps into templated tasks
acceptance_criteria: Cheflet service runs locally and returns a runbook-task bundle for all three probes
Bundle includes risk_level and approval_required metadata
Console shows suggestions panel with cheflet output and a link to the generated bundle
Runlet-runner refuses high-risk auto-execute and honors approval_required flag
Telemetry events appear in the ops dashboard within 5 minutes of invocation
Security review completed and sign-off attached to the ticket
progress_updates: 2026-03-11: Spike completed — prototype probes implemented in a dev branch; basic mapping from probe results to tasks verified against existing runbook snippets
2026-03-12: RFC posted in #eng-infra; early feedback recommends conservative defaults and explicit approver flows for any state-changing steps
2026-03-13: Design sync with Console team — agreed on cheflet suggestions panel UX and approve/execute button semantics
2026-03-14: PR #1122 opened with cheflet probe library and task bundle generator; CI green but needs integration tests
2026-03-15: Security pinged for threat model review; initial comments request audit trail persistence and KMS-backed signature for auto-exec approvals
review_feedback: PM (Rashid): prefer conservative defaults; prioritize read-only auto-actions first
Design (Ana): suggestion panel must show exact probes run, timestamps, and last successful probe to build trust
SRE (Katherine): require task bundle hash stored in audit-log and linkable to incident timeline
Security (Javier): KMS-signed approvals required for any task labeled risk_level=high; add rate limits to cheflet endpoints
notes: Planned first rollout in 'suggestion-only' mode to a 10% oncall cohort. If stable, enable read-only auto-actions (log collection, cache priming) for all oncall after sign-off. Coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams to ensure cheflet probes respect VPC constraints and do not leak metadata outside customer VPCs. Long-term: extend cheflet to synthesize multi-step canary remediation plans tied to rollout metadata and service-level runbooks.
risks: Accidental execution of high-risk remediation if approval gating is bypassed
False positives from probes causing noisy suggestions and alert fatigue
Data exposure if probes are run without VPC-aware credentials
